title: Syracuse Axon ALPR procurement baseline
summary: Issue #1903 bounded pass upgrades the Axon procurement evidence from secondary reporting to an official City of Syracuse January 27, 2026 STWG presentation. The city record states the proposed terms for 26 Axon readers, installation and maintenance, a 60-month term effective March 1, the first 12 months free, and a $422,636.28 not-to-exceed amount. It is governance/procurement evidence, not a recovered signed Master Service Agreement or proof of later technical configuration.

sources.title: Surveillance Technology Working Group Meeting #79 presentation
Syracuse lawmakers approve contract for Axon license plate readers, plan to block Flock Safety from city streets

evidence.claim: The January 27 City presentation describes an Axon agreement for 26 license-plate readers, including purchase, installation, maintenance, a 60-month term effective March 1, 2026, first 12 months free, and a $422,636.28 not-to-exceed amount.
The same presentation records that the Mayor waived the RFP process and that the Common Council was looking to schedule a committee meeting to discuss the agreement.
Independent local reporting says the Common Council later voted 7-1 on February 9, 2026 to approve the Axon license-plate-reader contract.

gaps: The attached signed/executed Axon Master Service Agreement and complete procurement attachment set are not recovered in this pass.
The official January 27 presentation describes proposed agreement terms and pre-vote governance state; it is not itself proof of execution.
The final 26-reader serial/location/ownership/activation inventory remains unresolved.
Native Axon retention, access, sharing, audit, role, and hotlist configuration remain unresolved.
No native evidence in this pass establishes migration of Flock data, users, cases, hotlists, credentials, or historical plate reads into Axon.
counterevidence: The January 27 City presentation says Common Council discussion was still pending, so it cannot by itself establish final approval or execution.
caveats: Central Current supplies independent evidence of the later 7-1 approval, but a press report is not a substitute for the signed MSA or final procurement file.

data.question: What authoritative public record establishes Syracuse's Axon ALPR procurement baseline without treating a proposal-stage presentation as the signed contract or as proof of system configuration?
data.method: Reconciled the current canonical Syracuse transition corpus with the City of Syracuse January 27, 2026 Surveillance Technology Working Group presentation and later independent reporting of the Common Council vote.
data.framework: Separate procurement/governance evidence from executed-contract evidence, technical configuration, observed deployment, and Flock-to-Axon migration.
data.scope: Syracuse Police Department Axon stationary-ALPR procurement terms and governance state from January 27 through February 9, 2026.
findings: The City of Syracuse January 27 STWG presentation describes an Axon agreement covering 26 license-plate readers plus purchase, installation, and maintenance.
The presentation records a March 1, 2026 effective date, 60-month period, first 12 months free, and total amount not to exceed $422,636.28.
The presentation records that the Mayor waived the RFP process and that Common Council discussion was still being scheduled at that stage.
Independent local reporting says Common Council subsequently voted 7-1 on February 9 to approve the Axon contract.
Neither the presentation nor the news report is the signed Master Service Agreement, so the canonical Axon-contract target remains unresolved.
conclusions: Syracuse's Axon procurement terms now have a primary City-government evidence anchor rather than relying only on secondary reporting.
The record materially narrows the contract target but does not complete it because the signed/executed MSA and full attachment set remain missing.
Nothing in this evidence proves final reader inventory, technical control configuration, or any Flock-to-Axon migration edge.
recommendations: Recover the executed Axon Master Service Agreement and all schedules/quotes/order forms referenced by the City presentation.
Recover the final 26-reader inventory with serials, locations, ownership, installation dates, activation timestamps, and status.
Recover native Axon role, access, sharing, audit, retention, hotlist, and regional Crime Analysis Center configuration/evidence.
Continue Flock-to-Axon migration testing only against native records.
counterarguments: A later council approval does not prove the precise executed document set matched every proposal-stage term without amendment.
A procurement record cannot establish that policy controls were technically configured or consistently enforced.
limitations: This pass recovered an official proposal/governance presentation and independent vote reporting, not the executed contract file or native configuration exports.
unresolved: Where is the signed Axon Master Service Agreement and its complete schedules/order forms?
Did the executed terms preserve the exact 60-month, first-year-free, and $422,636.28 terms?
What are the final serial/location/activation records for all 26 Axon stationary readers?
What native configuration and audit evidence implements the published Policy 427 controls?
Is there any native evidence of Flock-to-Axon user, data, case, hotlist, or historical-read migration?
